html:
Josephine de Beauharnais, born Marie-Josephe Rose Tascher de La Pagerie on a sugar plantation at Les Trois-Ilets in Martinique in 1763, became the first wife of Napoleon and Empress of the French.

She went to France at sixteen to marry the noble Alexandre de Beauharnais, who was guillotined in the Terror of the Revolution. She married Napoleon in 1796 and was crowned with him in 1804. Unable to give him an heir, she was divorced in 1809.

Many in Martinique hold her responsible for Napoleon's restoring of slavery in the French colonies in 1802, which Louis Delgres died resisting, though historians debate her part. Her statue in Fort-de-France was beheaded in 1991 and later torn down. The estate where she was born is a museum, near the plantations of the island.
sum: Josephine de Beauharnais, born Marie-Josephe Rose Tascher de La Pagerie on a sugar plantation at Les Trois-Ilets in Martinique in 1763, became the first wife of Napoleon and Empress of the French.
